input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Paragraph 8(h) is a mutual assignment clause that already gives AP the key protections: AP may assign without Kubient's consent to any affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all of the relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. The termination provisions (paragraph 4(a)-(b)) are limited to convenience after the Initial Term, material breach and insolvency; there is no change-of-control trigger, no deemed-assignment language and no Kubient right to terminate or re-price on an AP change of control, so none of the walk-away conditions are present. This meets the playbook fallback (mutual assignment with successor carve-out and a reasonableness standard for other assignments); pressing for the asymmetric preferred formulation (Kubient consent-only plus a competitor bar) would be disproportionate given the balanced bargain already struck, so no redline is proposed.
